---
title: "Exact Pareto fronts for MultiZenoTravel"
subtitle: "Blueprint: the theory note and its Lean formalization"
author: "Alexandre Quemy"
format:
  pdf:
    pdf-engine: xelatex
    documentclass: article
    papersize: a4
    geometry: [margin=2.2cm]
    # STIX Two from TeX Live's static OTF files (by file name, so that bold and italic resolve;
    # the system font is variable and would lose its bold). Covers Greek and the note's symbols.
    mainfont: STIXTwoText
    mainfontoptions:
      - Extension=.otf
      - UprightFont=*-Regular
      - BoldFont=*-Bold
      - ItalicFont=*-Italic
      - BoldItalicFont=*-BoldItalic
    mathfont: STIXTwoMath-Regular.otf
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
    number-sections: false
    colorlinks: true
    include-in-header:
      - tex/provenance.tex
      - text: |
          % STIX Two Text has no arrows or inequalities: in running text take them from the
          % math font; in code (JuliaMono, the monospace family) keep the font's own glyph.
          \usepackage{newunicodechar}
          \makeatletter
          \newcommand{\zs@sym}[2]{\ifmmode #1\else
            \edef\zs@fam{\f@family}\edef\zs@tt{\ttdefault}%
            \ifx\zs@fam\zs@tt\symbol{#2}\else\ensuremath{#1}\fi\fi}
          \newunicodechar{→}{\zs@sym{\rightarrow}{"2192}}
          \newunicodechar{←}{\zs@sym{\leftarrow}{"2190}}
          \newunicodechar{≥}{\zs@sym{\geq}{"2265}}
          \newunicodechar{≤}{\zs@sym{\leq}{"2264}}
          \newunicodechar{≠}{\zs@sym{\neq}{"2260}}
          \newunicodechar{↗}{\zs@sym{\nearrow}{"2197}}
          \makeatother
    code-overflow: wrap
---

This document is the PDF form of the blueprint at <https://quemy.info/ZenoSolver/proofs.html>. It
follows the theory note `doc/theory/exact-front.md` of the ZenoSolver repository
(<https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver>) statement by statement: the statement, the note's proof,
and the Lean declarations of `lean/ZenoFront` with their status. The status follows the claim
ledger `claims.toml`: *machine-checked* means that Lean proves every assertion of the statement,
with no axiom beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; *parts in Lean* that it proves
part of it, and a line says what is missing; *Lean definition* marks definitions; *informal* means
the statement is not in Lean.
